newsitem.title: GERMANY: GERMANY'S REXRODT - "NORMALISATION" IN DOLLAR RISE.
newsitem.headline: GERMANY'S REXRODT - "NORMALISATION" IN DOLLAR RISE.

text.p: German Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said Friday the dollar's rise against the deutschemark over the past few months represented a normalisation of exchange rates between the two currencies.

"What we've experienced in the last few months is a normalisation," Rexrodt told Germany's ARD television. "We have returned to relations between currencies which applied between the deutschemark and the dollar for a long time."
Rexrodt was speaking on ARD's Tagesthemen nightly news magazine programme.
A German government spokesman said earlier this week that the U.S. currency's recent strength was due to strong speculative impulses and that Bonn saw no reason to change its foreign exchange policy.
The weakness of the mark has helped many big export- dependent German companies and helped fuel recent rises on the Frankfurt stock exchange.

Over the past few months, the U.S unit has risen to levels unseen in the 1990s, driven by a strong U.S economy. Concerns about European monetary union have also played a part in the mark's weakness, market participants have said.
